attachments.origin_landmark: ischial tuberosity, superolateral facet of the upper area (flat membranous tendon of semimembranosus, lateral to the conjoint tendon of the other two hamstrings)
attachments.insertion_landmark: posteromedial tibial condyle (+ oblique popliteal ligament, popliteus fascia)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band -- for where this band lies along the muscle, see motor_endplate_zones

functional_compartments.function_note: Largest PCSA of the hamstring group; broad flat proximal tendon distinguishes its architecture from semitendinosus's round cord-like tendon.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset; Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: the medial and lateral femoral condyles
motor_endplate_zones.notes: This line runs DISTAL to PROXIMAL, so 20-40% lies in the distal part of the thigh -- which matches the clinic's own probe placement on the distal third of the posterior medial thigh. REFERENCE LINE DISCREPANCY: the review cited here states the 0% landmark as the femoral condyles, but the primary study it synthesises (Rha DW et al., Clin Anat 29(6):746-751 (2016), doi:10.1002/ca.22735, retrieved via PubMed) states the line as running from the medial and lateral TIBIAL condyles to the ischial tuberosity. Those landmarks are a few centimetres apart, which shifts every percentage on this line. The review's wording is kept because it is what the cited source says; confirm against the primary paper before measuring a patient.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the distal third of the posterior thigh, medial portion.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial to adductor magnus, which lies on the femoral cortex; semitendinosus lies lateral to it at this level.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: At the distal third, two muscle masses appear over adductor magnus: semimembranosus medial, semitendinosus lateral.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Contributes to excessive knee flexion in gait. Injection improves knee extension and anterior pelvic tilt and increases the rate of muscle lengthening.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites
